display.purpose: The one h1, centred, assembled a line at a time.

headline.purpose: Every section heading and the closing panel's.

title.purpose: A feature name, a step title, a footer column head.

lede.purpose: The paragraph under a headline. 34ch in the hero, 44ch in a section head.

body.purpose: Feature copy, step bodies, tile names. 36-38ch.

label.purpose: A fact's term, a footer column head. Sentence case, never stacked above a heading.

mono.purpose: Step numbers, dimensions, counts, search values. Tabular figures always.

shadows.name: shadow-sm
shadows.purpose: Resting: a button, a flag, a search bar.

shadows.name: shadow
shadows.purpose: Lifted: a gallery tile, a hovered primary button, the stuck nav pill.

shadows.name: shadow-lg
shadows.purpose: Carrying a picture: the showpiece, the walkthrough art, a paired render.

shadows.name: stroke-light
shadows.purpose: The inset hairline on a ghost control. Never combined with an ambient shadow on a card.

shadows.name: stroke-dark
shadows.purpose: The inset hairline on a ghost button on the dark panel.

shadows.name: contact
shadows.purpose: Under a character's feet, cast from the figure rather than painted on the floor.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The page's one curve. Everything covers most of its distance immediately and lands slowly.

motion.name: rise
motion.purpose: The arrival state. Opacity 620ms, transform 760ms, blur 620ms.

motion.name: stagger
motion.purpose: A group arrives as a group, one item a beat behind the last.

motion.name: righting
motion.purpose: The page's one 3D movement, spent on the first screenshot.

motion.name: loop-marquee
motion.purpose: The two gallery strips. One of the only two sanctioned loops.

motion.name: loop-trace
motion.purpose: The running 555 trace. The other sanctioned loop.

motion.name: reduced
motion.value: opacity 1, transform none, filter none, transition none, animation none
motion.purpose: Everything resolves to its final state; every loop stops rather than slows.

narrative.overview:
This is the category convention — the clean, light, modern product page — executed at the craft level of the two pages the product owner pinned, and nothing more clever than that. There is no concept and no own-world. What makes it work is not an idea, it is three things the first attempt did not have: density, motion and photography. Sections are short and close together and every one has something in it worth looking at. The page arrives rather than loading. And the product is shown as a photograph of itself at full size, never as a drawing of itself.

The material is warm paper, not white. Every neutral is pulled a few degrees towards it: an off-white ground with yellow in it, a warm near-black ink, oatmeal rules, brown shadows that are wide and faint rather than tight and dark. Against that, the renders are dark — near-black panels in a generous radius with a wide soft shadow under them — and the one cool thing on the page is the accent blue, which is the logo's. A cool accent on a warm ground reads as ink rather than as a highlighter, which is the whole reason the blue is left alone while everything around it is warmed.

Depth comes from shadow, never from a line. Surfaces lift; borders divide content. Nothing on the page does both, and a card that needs an outline to exist is a card that has not been lifted far enough. Four characters live on this page — Rig, Dot, Sixteen and Seg — one to a section, each standing on a drawn floor, each lit in the colour the part it is made of really emits.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper ground (#FDFBF7), warm near-black ink, oatmeal rules, brown shadows
One accent (blue #1E6FFF) for intent and selection; amber reserved for energised
Dark renders at full size in generous radii — the product photographed, not drawn
Depth is a shadow; nothing has both a shadow and a border
Every corner is rounded, from 10px on a row to a full pill on every control
One motion grammar: rise 18px, blur 6px, fade, one curve, staggered
Two loops on the page, and both of them carry content
Figures stand on drawn floors, one to a section, never beside running text
Every count on the page is read out of the repository at runtime

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Blue #1E6FFF is the only accent on the page, and it means intent or selection. Amber is reserved and means energised — current in a wire, a lit dot, a hot tip — and it never decorates. A third colour is how this kind of page starts to look cheap. Audit test: point at any blue pixel and say in four words what was intended or picked; point at any amber pixel and name what is energised.

rules.name: The Warm Neutral Rule
rules.body: Every neutral carries the paper's warmth. A grey with no yellow in it, a pure white surface, or a black shadow is outside the palette. The blue is the one thing that stays cool, and it stays cool on purpose.

rules.name: The Measurement Rule
rules.body: Monospace carries numbers and measurements only — step numbers, dimensions, part counts, search values. Tabular figures are on wherever a number can change, so a count that animates up does not shuffle the line it sits in. Prose, headings and button labels are never mono.

rules.name: The Tight-At-Size Rule
rules.body: Tracking closes as type grows and opens as it shrinks. A headline at default tracking is the single clearest sign this page was not set by anyone.

rules.name: The Counted Number Rule
rules.body: A number on the page is read from the thing it counts, never typed into the markup. The catalogue count and the build count are imported at runtime and animate up from zero once; until they arrive the row holds its height with a dash so nothing below it moves. The page once said 172 parts in two places while the catalogue held 194.

rules.name: The One Head Rule
rules.body: Every section uses the same head block — 44ch, one margin below, centred or not. Three sections each owning a private copy of it is how a page ends up with three head alignments and no rule behind any of them.

rules.name: The Depth-Is-A-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Borders divide content; shadows lift a surface. Nothing on this page has both. A border on a card, a tile or a control is a defect — the only borders in the system are the 1px dividers between rows and columns, which separate content and lift nothing.

rules.name: The Shadow-Grows-With-The-Hand Rule
rules.body: A hover raises the shadow one step and the element by 1px, or 3px for a build tile. It never scales: a button that scales on hover moves the text under the cursor.

rules.name: The One Grammar Rule
rules.body: Everything that moves goes through ui/motion.tsx and shares its one curve, one distance and one direction. A new section does not bring its own entrance.

rules.name: The Loops Carry Content Rule
rules.body: The only loops on the page are the ones whose motion is the content: the two gallery strips and the running trace. A decorative loop — a pulsing badge, a floating card, a bobbing icon — is not part of this system.

rules.name: The Counted Tally Rule
rules.body: A number only animates up when it was read off something real. A figure that counts up to a value nobody can check is a slot machine.

rules.name: The Drawn Floor Rule
rules.body: Every figure stands on a drawn floor and is never placed in a margin beside running text. A figure in the gutter next to a paragraph is a sticker in the whitespace: it has no floor, nothing to do, and on a narrow window it lands on the text. One to a section, never a row of them.

rules.name: The Photograph Rule
rules.body: No flat drawing of the product stands in for a photograph of it. Every product image comes out of tools/shoot-cine.mjs, shot from inside the running app: close, off-axis, near the height of the subject, lit from the side, framed off-centre. Three frames keep the editor's own chrome, because a page that only ever shows the render never shows the product. Diagrams of ideas are drawn; the thing being sold is photographed.

rules.name: The Nothing-To-Operate Rule
rules.body: No section requires a click before it says anything. A visitor three screens into a product page has not agreed to operate a widget. A demonstration is driven by the scrollbar.

dos: Do keep blue #1E6FFF for intent and selection, and keep amber for energised — current, a lit dot, a hot tip. Nothing else is coloured.
Do carry depth in a shadow: wide, faint, brown, one of the three steps.
Do put every photograph of the product in a dark rounded frame at 16/10 or 4/3, at full size, with the widest shadow under it.
Do round every corner, and make every control a full pill.
Do move everything through ui/motion.tsx: rise 18px, blur 6px, fade, cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), staggered within a group, once on entry.
Do read every count off the repository at runtime and let it tally up from zero.
Do stand a figure on a drawn floor, one to a section, with room around it.
Do warm every neutral towards the paper and leave the blue cool.
Do resolve everything to its final state under prefers-reduced-motion, with nothing hidden and no loop running.
Do keep the 1240px measure unless a screenshot of the three-column editor is in the section, which is the one reason to take 1480px.
donts: Don't give an element both a shadow and a border. Borders divide content; shadows lift surfaces.
Don't introduce a third colour, or use the accent to tint a surface for mood or to mark a section.
Don't use the render's amber #FFB020 on warm paper — it is illegible there; #D98500 is the paper rendition.
Don't draw the product. A flat SVG vignette of a desk or a bench standing in for a photograph is the specific failure this page was rebuilt to remove.
Don't add a second motion grammar, a loop that carries no content, or a scroll animation that replays when the reader comes back up.
Don't spend a second piece of 3D movement. The budget is one, and the first screenshot has it.
Don't type a number into the page that something in the repository counts.
Don't put a figure in a margin beside running text, or line several of them up in a row.
Don't make the reader operate a control before a section will say anything.
Don't scale a button on hover; nudge its arrow instead.
Don't set prose, headings or button labels in monospace.
Don't stack a label above a heading. The labels here name a fact, head a footer column or caption a picture; there are no kickers on this page.
Don't let a section invent its own head block, alignment or max-width.
